name: blast-drill-plan-ui
description: Visual verification of drill plan UI: grid creation, hole markers, camera orbit, replace grid. #553: confirming a grid queues one drill_hole PendingAction per hole instead of writing holes instantly — holes sit ordered (ghosts) in plannedDrillHoles until a staffed driller/drill_rig actually drills each one, landing it in drillHoles.

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551): a driller with blasting + drill_rig licence, plus an unmanned drill_rig, are hired/purchased for free at game-open — exactly what #553's automatic drill dispatch needs.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:3 spacing:5 depth:6 start:12,12
steps.description: The grid tool's spacing stepper defaults to 3m (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts) — dragging this rectangle at that default would compute a different rows/cols than this command declares. Two increment clicks on the strip's own spacing stepper (data-field="spacing", added so this is reachable at all) raise it 3->5 before dragging (round(10/5)+1=3 cols, round(5/5)+1=2 rows), so the click reaches the exact grid the command names. #553: confirming the grid queues 6 drill_hole PendingActions and pushes 6 PlannedHoles into plannedDrillHoles — none are drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after confirm. Hole count kept modest (6, not the larger patterns used pre-#553) so the staffed roster's ongoing maintenance/fuel costs (no income in this scenario) don't run the site into BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS territory before the plan finishes draining below.

expect.note: 2 rows x 3 cols = 6 holes ordered (ghosts), matching the command's declared pattern now that the click actually uses spacing:5 — none drilled yet (#553).

steps.description: #553: partial drilling — the staffed driller/drill_rig has had time to land some, but not all, of the 6 ordered holes (40 ticks covers travel from the staffed spawn near the origin plus a couple of holes' drill duration, with several holes still left to go — see computeDrillHoleDurationTicks/DRILL_HOLE_BASE_DURATION_TICKS). Mid-drilling screenshot for the visual channel to inspect the ghost/drilled split (undrilled holes still shown as ghosts, drilled ones as real holes). Tick counts here are a first estimate from the spec's own duration formula and staffed spawn offsets — tune once real timing is observed running against the implementation, same as any other scenario's tick padding.

expect.note: Some holes have landed in drillHoles (real) while others remain in plannedDrillHoles (ghosts) — proves the split actually works, not just that ticking doesn't crash.

steps.description: #553: drain the rest of the plan — every ordered hole eventually lands. Kept well under the staffed site's own bankruptcy-grace window (observed ~259 ticks with no income) since this is a single unconditional tick command, not a loop that stops once the plan finishes.

expect.note: All 6 holes have landed — none lost, none left ordered forever.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:8 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:8 depth:6 start:20,20 BlastWorkshop auto-advances Drill -> Charge once holes exist, so re-using the grid tool needs an explicit click back to the Drill tab ([data-step="1"]) first. The spacing stepper also carries its value over from the first grid above (now 5, not the 3m default) — 3 more increments reach this step's declared spacing:8 (round(8/8)+1=2 cols/rows, matching rows:2 cols:2) before dragging. depth corrected from 10 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. #553: confirming a new grid cancels/wipes the fully-drilled previous plan (drillHoles) and the fresh 4 holes start out ordered, not drilled — holeCount drops back to 0.
